about: MessagePack-CSharp profile policy. First matching area wins; content rules only look at added lines.

areas.why: Reads untrusted bytes at runtime in every consumer: crashes, DoS and data corruption land in production.
Public attributes shipped to every consumer. Each addition is a permanent API commitment.
Emits code into consumer builds. Bugs show up as wrong serialization or build breaks in user code.
Shipped library code outside the core runtime.
Not shipped. Risk is weak tests, not runtime behaviour. Package references added here are still raised by the dependency-change rule.
Supply chain and build integrity: what gets compiled and shipped.
No policy area matched. Unknown is not low risk.

content_rules.why: Manual memory access. An off-by-one here is a buffer over-read, not just a wrong value.
Type names from the payload can choose which code runs (deserialization gadgets).
Touches the library's own DoS and hash-flooding defences.
Decompression of untrusted input (size bombs, length checks).
Sizes read from the payload drive allocations and loops.
New or changed public member in a shipped runtime package: an API compatibility decision.
A dependency was added or bumped: supply-chain review, and is it in scope?
CI definitions can exfiltrate secrets or skip checks.

tier_meaning.T0: Evidence check: the owner reads the dossier and spot-checks one verified claim (about 5 min).
tier_meaning.T1: Focused read: the owner reads only the listed hunks plus the dossier (about 15 min).
tier_meaning.T2: Full read: the owner reads every line of this area; for security rules, a security champion co-signs.

generated_pairs.why: T4 templates and their generated C# must change together.
